findings.summary: Signed cash medians and 'the completing side pays' are read as a completion premium or as recipients forgoing money, but cash is the price of the deed the completer receives, and list-price comparisons show no buyer-side completion markup.
findings.evidence: checks/offer_checks.py: the completing side receives a deed in 429 of 429 one-sided offers. Pure cash bids for one's own completion median 1.32x list (n=134) vs 1.38x in non-completing purchases (n=178); unmortgaged 1.57 vs 1.50; opening 1.40 vs 1.36; later 1.31 vs 1.43. Seller asks for a recipient-completing deed 1.63x (n=93) vs 1.08x non-completing (n=117), shrinking to 2.31 vs 1.82 unmortgaged and 2.21 vs 1.85 among later offers (checks/list_price_robustness.py). List price ignores bundle composition and position.
findings.check_status: performed_by_opus_review (retained offer ledger + board prices); Astra F2/A1 reach the premium objection without the list-price test
findings.resolution: Replace with: cash usually flows to the side giving up the completing deed, as in any purchase; relative to board prices, bids for one's own completion were not higher than other bids, while asks for a recipient-completing deed were somewhat higher in every split examined; none of these holds price, position and portfolio fixed. Remove 373/429 from abstracts.
